news.title: GCCs may lease 35-40 million sq ft office space annually over next two years: Report
news.para: Global capability centres have leased about 118 million sq ft of Grade-A office space across India’s top seven cities since 2021, accounting for 37% of overall office demand, according to Colliers India. GCCs leased 16.6 million sq ft in H1 2026, with Bengaluru and Hyderabad accounting for over 60% of demand.

news.title: Make sure Indiramma houses are built only in residential areas: Telangana CM to officials
news.para: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy directed officials to build Indiramma housing scheme houses within Hyderabad's core urban region. This ensures beneficiaries can access livelihood opportunities and commute to work easily. The government plans to construct 7,680 flats in the first phase across several assembly constituencies. Each multi-storey flat will have 525 square feet built-up area, with land cost borne by the government.

news.title: Prestige Group acquires 2.35-acre land in Mumbai's Mulund for ₹110.75 crore
news.para: The transaction was executed through Prestige Mulund Realty Pvt Ltd, which acquired the property from Shamvik Glasstech Pvt Ltd and General Glass Company Pvt Ltd. The deal was registered on July 16, with the buyer paying stamp duty of Rs 6.64 crore, according to property registration documents accessed through CRE Matrix, realty data analytics platform.

news.title: Karnataka government to crack down on developers overloading power grid
news.para: Energy officials are cracking down on large projects overloading Bengaluru's electricity network. Developers who failed to create mandatory electrical infrastructure will face action. Nearly 45 such projects have been identified and issued notices by the government. These projects are liable to pay a penalty of ten percent of their cost. Continued non-compliance could lead to disconnection of power supply.

news.title: Chennai developers seek clarification from CMDA on FSI rules along metro corridor
news.para: Developers have asked the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority for policy clarification.  Uncertainty over concessional Premium FSI charges delays project approvals.  Credai Chennai seeks eligibility for sites partially within the 500-meter metro corridor zone.  They request the concession not be denied due to road frontage outside the limit.  A uniform interpretation will reduce delays and promote development along metro corridors.

news.title: Pune: Cheating FIR against 22 for using forged PMRDA & PMC documents to register sale deeds
news.para: Ambegaon police registered a case against twenty-two people for cheating the government.  Seven builders and developers allegedly used forged PMRDA and PMC documents.  These forged documents were used to register twenty-two property sale deeds.  The investigation is ongoing, and more cases may be registered soon.  State registration officials are seeking a detailed probe into suspected fake documents.

news.title: Realty United Infra's director arrested for land fraud in Indore
news.para: A real estate director was arrested in Indore for alleged fraud. Anita Gehlot, director of Realty United Infra Private Limited, is accused of cheating a woman. She allegedly sold a government-mortgaged plot using forged documents. The complainant lost Rs 18.75 lakh in the fraudulent sale transaction. Police are investigating if other buyers were also defrauded.

news.title: Onida looks to monetise realty assets for revival
news.para: Onida Electronics is monetising its real estate portfolio to raise crucial funds.  The company plans to revive its iconic television brand and compete effectively.  Three land parcels, including its Mumbai headquarters, are being evaluated for sale.  Operations at the Wada manufacturing facility have been discontinued and exited.  Television production will now be outsourced to contract manufacturers.

news.title: Dalmia Bharat's profit falls 51.4% to ₹192 crore in Q1 FY27
news.para: Dalmia Bharat's net profit fell fifty-one point four percent year-on-year in the June quarter. Revenue from operations increased seven percent to three thousand eight hundred ninety crore rupees. Exceptional costs of one hundred eighty-two crore impacted the company's quarterly results. Sales volume grew nine percent to seven point six million tonnes during the period. Yatin Malhotra will become the new Chief Financial Officer on August first.

news.title: Lodha Developers’ net profit more than doubles to ₹1,373.10 crore in Q1 FY27
news.para: Lodha Developers consolidated total income increased 40.6 per cent to ₹5,096.70 crore during the quarter. Pre-sales stood at ₹4,629 crore, while collections rose 46 per cent year-on-year to ₹4,205 crore.

news.title: ACC's net profit declines 61% to ₹147 crore in Q1 FY27
news.para: ACC's consolidated total income fell 8.4 per cent to ₹5,861 crore during the quarter. Cement sales volume stood at 10 million tonnes, while the share of green power increased to 31 per cent. During the quarter, ACC extended inter-corporate deposits aggregating ₹3,900 crore to its holding company, Ambuja Cements.

news.title: Orient Cement's profit declines 62.4%, revenue slides to ₹604 crore in Q1 FY27
news.para: Orient Cement's net profit dropped sixty-two percent in the June quarter. Revenue from operations also saw a thirty percent decrease during the same period. The company acquired a nine percent stake in Vena Energy KN Wind Power. This acquisition will allow Orient Cement to use renewable electricity. The deal is expected to be completed by August 2026.

news.title: Primus Senior Living, HDFC Capital form ₹2,000 crore senior living platform
news.para: Primus Senior Living and HDFC Capital have partnered to create a ₹2,000 crore senior living platform. The platform plans to deploy ₹1,000 crore in FY27 across six projects and the full corpus over two years.

news.title: Beyond insolvency: Rethinking resolution strategies for India’s stressed real estate sector
news.para: Stuck housing projects highlight challenges with India's insolvency code.  The current system often delays resolutions and weakens project values.  Reverse insolvency offers a promising completion-centric path for troubled developments.  This approach focuses on finishing homes rather than just recovering money.  Better coordination and timely funding are crucial for successful project revival.

news.title: Patna civic body's property tax collection rises by 13.9% from April to July
news.para: The civic body attributed the rise to sustained public outreach and awareness campaigns aimed to encourage timely payments. Officials said PMC has been contacting property owners daily by telephone and using other platforms to spread awareness about meeting tax deadlines.

news.title: Pace of work slow despite NBCC takeover, say Supertech homebuyers
news.para: Supertech Ltd launched several residential and commercial projects in Noida, Greater Noida, the Yamuna Expressway region, Gurgaon and other cities, mostly between 2010 and 2012. Delays in completing these projects led to defaults on repayments to financial creditors.

news.title: Gurugram: 13 years on, no handover, Haryana RERA orders ₹50 lakh compensation to buyer
news.para: Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority ordered a developer to pay compensation. The homebuyer booked a unit in 2010, with possession due in 2012. The project remained incomplete for over six years past the promised delivery date. The authority awarded compensation for delay and mental harassment. The developer must also pay litigation costs and interest on the awarded sum.

news.title: Bengaluru builder to raze shaky tower three months after getting occupancy certificate
news.para: An 18-floor apartment tower in Bengaluru will be demolished soon. This decision comes after the building was found to be tilting significantly. The builder plans to reconstruct the entire 49-unit tower within two years. Buyers will have to wait longer for their dream homes. Authorities are reviewing the occupancy certificate and ensuring nearby structures remain safe.

news.title: Bengaluru development body imposes curbs on revised building plans after OCs
news.para: Bangalore Development Authority has restricted approving revised building plans after occupancy certificates are issued.  A new circular mandates owner consent for modifications where third-party rights exist.  This order follows a legal challenge by residents of HM Tambourine apartment complex.  The residents contested a modified sanction plan approved without their consent.  This move aims to protect apartment owners' rights and development potential.

news.title: Odisha REAT dismisses promoter’s appeal against ORERA order
news.para: The Odisha Real Estate Appellate Tribunal dismissed a promoter's appeal against an ORERA order.  The tribunal upheld directions to protect apartment owners' interests in a residential project.  Deficiencies in promised amenities and structural issues were noted during inspections.  The promoter must rectify defects and complete all formalities within three months.  Common areas will be maintained by the promoter until formal handover to the association.
